questions.prompt: A product license is assigned to the assigned-membership security group Parent. User1 is a direct member of Child, and Child is a member of Parent. Direct user members of Parent receive the product after processing completes, but User1 does not. Seats are available and User1 has a valid usage location. What explains the difference?

options.text: Group-based licensing processes direct user members rather than nested user membership.
options.explanation: User1 is reachable only through Child. Nested membership does not qualify for the license assigned to Parent.

options.text: Group-based licensing processes group owners rather than group members.
options.explanation: The product is assigned to direct user members. Ownership is not the membership path used here.

options.text: Group-based licensing has stopped because the product has no available seats.
options.explanation: Available seats are explicitly confirmed. Capacity cannot explain the difference.

options.text: Group-based licensing is still processing all direct members of Parent.
options.explanation: Processing has completed and direct members received the product. Waiting cannot make nested membership eligible.

questions.prompt: User1 has the same product license assigned directly and through Group1. An administrator removes the product from Group1 and confirms processing is complete. The direct assignment is still active, and there are no other assignment paths. Which state should the administrator expect for User1?

options.text: The product remains assigned through the direct assignment.
options.explanation: The active direct assignment remains a source of the product after the group path is removed.

options.text: The product is unassigned because removing any source removes all sources.
options.explanation: The group and direct assignments are separate paths. The direct path remains active.

options.text: The product remains assigned through Group1 because direct assignments take precedence.
options.explanation: The group path was removed. A direct assignment does not preserve a removed group assignment.

options.text: The direct assignment is converted into an assignment inherited from Group1.
options.explanation: Removing the group path does not convert the remaining direct path into group inheritance.

questions.prompt: A new user works in Germany, where the selected product is available. Group license processing reports a usage-location error despite available seats. The user profile contains country = Germany and usageLocation = US. Which user property should an administrator correct to match the verified place of service use before reprocessing?

options.explanation: Licensing checks service availability using usageLocation. DE represents the verified location in this scenario.
The profile country field is separate from usageLocation. Changing it leaves the licensing property incorrect.
Preferred language controls language preferences. It does not replace the licensing location.
Office location describes the workplace. It does not correct usageLocation.
